review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the filtration simp setup in SpectralObject.lean (filtrationEInt_*, filtrationFunctor_obj, filtrationFunctor_obj_coe, filtrationFunctor_map_bot_top). I checked Mathlib's Subobject.bot_arrow and botCoeIsoZero, and the helper lemmas in TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/Subobject.lean. Nothing was run. Both findings are modest. I did not check the other uses of these lemmas across the repo, and I did not test that the proposed changes compile. The remaining proofs in the file are mostly manual rewriting with existing simp lemmas, and I found no loop or competing-rule problem.

findings.excerpt: have hz : (filtrationFunctor F hF).map (homOfLE (bot_le : (⊥ : EInt) ≤ a)) = 0 := by
findings.problem: The simp interface lacks a general lemma saying that a transition map out of `⊥` in `filtrationFunctor` is zero. SpectralObject.lean has only the special case `filtrationFunctor_map_bot_top`, which is the target `⊤` and is not `@[simp]`. The Stabilization proof therefore re-proves the statement for general `a` as a local `have hz`. It repeats the same `rw [filtrationFunctor_obj, filtrationEInt_bot]` and `botCoeIsoZero` argument that appears in `filtrationFunctor_map_bot_top`. Other uses with a target other than `⊤` would copy it again.
findings.proposed_change: In SpectralObject.lean, replace `filtrationFunctor_map_bot_top` with a general lemma such as `filtrationFunctor_map_bot {a : EInt} (f : (⊥ : EInt) ⟶ a) : (filtrationFunctor F hF).map f = 0`. Tag it `@[simp]`: the LHS is `map` applied to a morphism out of `⊥` and the RHS is `0`, so it cannot loop. Keep `filtrationFunctor_map_bot_top` as a corollary or delete it. Then `hz` becomes `filtrationFunctor_map_bot F hF _`, or `by simp`, and the local proof disappears.
findings.benefit: Expressions of the form `(filtrationFunctor F hF).map (homOfLE bot_le)` normalize to `0` under `simp`. Readers no longer see the zero-object argument duplicated in two files, and downstream cokernel computations can use `simp` instead of hand-built `hz` facts.

findings.problem: `filtrationFunctor_obj` is `@[simp]` and rewrites `(filtrationFunctor F hF).obj a` to `(filtrationEInt F a : _)`. `filtrationEInt_coe` is also `@[simp]` and rewrites `filtrationEInt F ↑n` to `F n`. So `simp` already normalizes `(filtrationFunctor F hF).obj ↑n` to `F n`. The separate, non-simp `filtrationFunctor_obj_coe` is a redundant spelling of a rewrite that `simp` already performs. The proof then uses it through manual `rw` plus `exact h` instead of the simp normal form. Having both the simp chain and an unattributed lemma for the same rewrite is confusing, because it is unclear which form is canonical.
findings.proposed_change: Either drop `filtrationFunctor_obj_coe`, or mark it `@[simp]` as the one-step form of the existing chain. For this proof, `simpa using h` should replace the `rw [filtrationFunctor_obj_coe]; exact h` step (not compiled).
findings.benefit: There is one canonical simp normal form (`F n`) for the filtration functor at integer indices. Proofs here and in other files can use `simp` or `simpa` instead of choosing between `rw` lemmas, and the interface has one fewer redundant lemma.
